steps.label: Firewall alert
steps.sub: traffic spike — backup job, or exfiltration?

steps.label: IDS alert
steps.sub: odd command — admin script, or recon?

steps.label: Needs context
steps.sub: an analyst has to resolve the ambiguity first

eyebrow: A honeypot alert has no ambiguity
code:
Firewall alert:  "could be legitimate traffic that looks bad"
Honeypot alert:  "no legitimate explanation exists, by design"

=> extremely low false-positive rate
caption: The alert isn't asking 'does this look bad?' — it's reporting a fact that is already bad.

steps.label: Narrow visibility
steps.sub: sees only what actually touches it

steps.label: Not comprehensive
steps.sub: not a replacement for IDS/EDR coverage

steps.label: Still worth it
steps.sub: a trustworthy alert beats a thousand noisy ones

code:
SOC triages ~10,000 firewall/IDS alerts/day
Honeypot fires ~2 times/month

Every single honeypot hit => immediate investigation
(trusted before anything else is even checked)
caption: Its value was never volume — it's that when it finally speaks, it's always telling the truth.
